reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Bag of Tricks first, taking the option to spend 3 Sparks and place 3 Bombs dealing 5 against Nibbit. Then I played Spirited Away for 12 Block. This uses all 2 Energy, spends all 3 Sparks, and leaves the enemy’s 12 damage fully blocked.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing Bag of Tricks for only 1 Bomb and then Spirited Away. That would preserve 3 Sparks and still block the full 12 damage, but it would deal only 5 damage instead of 15. I also briefly considered Duck and Cover plus Run Away! for 9 Block, but that would take 3 damage and is strictly worse than Spirited Away for the same total Energy.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gives up the option to keep 3 Sparks unspent. It also gives up the lower-damage, lower-spark line of placing only 1 Bomb. In practice, the 3-Bomb option is refunded by Pounding Surprise when the Bombs detonate, so the main real cost is committing to the 3-Bomb choice rather than preserving the simpler 1-Bomb state.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. The enemy’s telegraphed 12 Attack is exactly what Spirited Away blocks, and the Bag of Tricks choice is driven by free damage and Spark refund rather than by the enemy’s intent. A different intent would not make the 1-Bomb option better, because the 3-Bomb option still deals more damage and returns the spent Sparks through the relic.

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
